newsitem.title: ISRAEL: First Intl Bank Q3 net up 63 pct.
newsitem.headline: First Intl Bank Q3 net up 63 pct.

text.p: First International, one of Israel's five largest banks, said the 63 percent increase in third-quarter net profit from a year earlier was due mainly to inflation accounting.

Inflation accounting also boosted the bank's nine-month net profit by 10.7 million shekels. However, changes in the tax treatment of foreign banking subsidiaries in the last year erased about 5.6 million shekels from net, First International said.
Based on its nine-month earnings, the bank's annualised net return on equity rose to 9.4 percent from 8.7 percent a year ago.

Income from financial activities rose 2.7 percent in the nine months due to increased lending activity and to wider financial margins. The bank said the 10.3 percent rise in operating income stemmed principally from increased foreign currency-trading activity.

Fee income from capital market activity continued to decline. However First International said its provident funds (long-term savings funds) had weathered the big wave of redemptions during the third quarter well.

"In the first nine months of 1996, net redemptions in the provident and advanced-education funds were just 387 million shekels, compared with redemptions for the overall sector of 11.07 billion," the bank said.
It attributed the small decline to the bank funds' relatively good returns and to stepped-up marketing.
First International said shareholders' equity grew to 1.98 billion shekels as of September 30 against 1.87 billion a year earlier.

Credit to the public rose to 21.88 billion shekels at the end of the quarter from 18.34 billion a year earlier, while deposits from the public reached 23.74 billion shekels from 20.85 billion shekels. Total assets rose to 29.84 billion shekels from 26.10 billion a year earlier.
